titleStmt.title: The patent investing Shang Han as King (of Lew Chew) in the thirteenth year of Kia-King.

div.head: The patent investing Shang Han as King (of Lew Chew) in the thirteenth year of Kia-King.
div.p: I, the sovereign Emperor, hereby make known My commands to Shang Han, a grandson of the King of Lew Chew in the Central Mount.

Whereas, your ancestors have for generations kept the outskirts of Our realm as a protective feudatory, sedulous to present their tribute at the proper time, and having all been honorable, worthy, and just persons, who have tried to follow that which is decorous, and maintain the proprieties of their stations, have thus approved themselves to Our constant commendation, and their illustrious fame has in consequence become known through all ranks of Our officers:

Now, therefore, having in course succeeded to the inheritance, you have sent your messengers to request Our commands. They knocked at Our frontier passes on their way, and have at last reached the court of ceremonies, whose officers have greeted them. Their strong desire was to reach this goal with their presents; hastening on their journey away from the waters where the sole-fish abounds. From those distant
outskirts where the clouds hide the horizon they have reverently brought your palm-leaf missive expressing your respectful feelings.

We, on Our part, now return, over land and water, Our silken (i. e., imperial) mandates to your rural hamlet, in order to invest you with the lawful succession. We shall continue Our patronage to your truly loyal family and to your descendants, as we now exhibit Our high regard by sending these letters patent, which will call forth your constant allegiance. How glorious your race be!

We have accordingly now commissioned Tsi Kwan, a revisor in the Han-lin Academy, as Our chief envoy, and Fei Tsz-Chang, an under secretary of the board of works, as the second, who are ordered to your country, and confer to you (on Our behalf) the dignity of King of Lew Chew in the Central Mount. By them We have sent to you and your Queen presents of silks, letters, &c., all of which you will respectfully regard as the expression of Our favor, and receive at their hands, with your attendants, according to the prescribed ritual. They will all, as the stately bamboo dresses itself in new foliage, give you increased honor. They are substantial tokens of regard given to those who come to Our palace; therefore, carefully arrange them, and cherish and preserve them as one does his girdle jewels. All your people will regard them as evidence that you emulate the glory of your predecessors in their rule. Therefore, regard their instructions with trembling docility, whereby your land will be prosperous and famous, and you be enriched with unchanging and peaceful blessings.
Hear, therefore, and respect Our special behest.

List of articles bestowed on the King of the state.—Two pieces imperial dragon satin; three pieces lustrous variegated satin; three pieces variegated blue satin; three pieces plain blue satin; two pieces changeable satin; two pieces plain satin; three pieces brocade; four pieces gauze; four pieces heavy curtain gauzefour pieces pongee.

List of articles bestowed on the Queen.—Two pieces lustrous variegated satin; two pieces blue; one piece violet; two pieces plain blue satin; one piece changeable satin; two pieces plain satin; two pieces brocade; four pieces gauze; four pieces heavy curtain gauze.
